answer_text:
(1) Simplify by canceling:
\[
96 \times 15 \div (45 \times 16)
=\frac{96}{16}\times\frac{15}{45}
=6\times \frac13
=2
\]

(2) The first product has \(100\) factors of \(125\), and the second has \(101\) factors of \(8\):
\[
125^{100}\times 8^{101}
\]
Group \(100\) of the \(8\)'s with the \(125\)'s:
\[
125^{100}\times 8^{100}\times 8
=(125\cdot 8)^{100}\times 8
=1000^{100}\times 8
\]
Since \(1000=10^3\),
\[
1000^{100}\times 8
=(10^3)^{100}\times 8
=10^{300}\times 8
=8\times 10^{300}
\]

(3) The sum is
\[
2+4+6+\cdots+100
\]
These are the first \(50\) even numbers, so
\[
2+4+\cdots+100
=2(1+2+\cdots+50)
=2\cdot \frac{50\cdot 51}{2}
=50\cdot 51
=2550
\]

\[
\boxed{2,\;8\times 10^{300},\;2550}
\]
